title: Decide What Data Can Tell You
core_invariant: Statistical evidence is a point estimate, an uncertainty interval, an effect size, a sample size, and stated assumptions together. A p-value is not the probability the null is true. Correlation is not identification. Cherry-picking among many comparisons is not a confirmatory test. Predict before simulating. Transfer without assistance.

stages.title: Frame the estimand before the test
stages.instructions: Read the M18 invariant and the checkout experiment: primary metric checkout_conversion, estimand variant_B_rate minus variant_A_rate, 95% interval, alpha 0.05, one planned comparison. Identify gate evidence: sampling-variation simulations, mean/median/variance in distribution context, analytic and bootstrap intervals, a useful hypothesis test, a refused causal claim from seasonal correlation, a cherry-pick diagnosis, and no-AI transfer. Generic WP-137 table and metric blocks; no custom frontend.

stages.title: Trace interval, bootstrap, and selection
stages.instructions: Read the inference helpers. Locate the unpooled standard error, the normal interval, the seeded bootstrap resampling unit, and any filter that keeps p < 0.05. Predict whether hiding the comparison family changes the reported story without changing the data.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Trace names estimand, resampling unit, and the selection line that creates a cherry-pick.

stages.title: Predict the interval, then compute B minus A
stages.instructions: Complete the experiment cycle on the generic runtime. (1) PREDICT the observable outcome before any numbers appear. (2) COMMIT the prediction so it cannot be edited. (3) EXECUTE / RUN the measurement. (4) OBSERVE structured WP-137 blocks. (5) SUBMIT / EXPLAIN any delta between prediction and observation. Given two binomial conversion counts, predict whether a 95% interval for B minus A includes zero. EXECUTE the unpooled standard error and normal interval. Emit a WP-137 metric of point estimate, SE, interval, and sample sizes plus a table of rates. Interpret compatible effect values without declaring proof of equality.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Prediction is sealed before execute; report includes estimate, interval, effect size, and n together.

stages.title: Diagnose a manufactured significant win
stages.instructions: Twenty independent null comparisons are generated; the table is filtered to p < 0.05. The seeded failure is cherry-picking. Predict the chance of at least one false positive, show the full comparison family, minimum p-value, selection line, and familywise false-positive rate. Repair by pre-specifying one primary comparison and a Bonferroni (or FDR) control before rerunning. Never use the failure procedure on real stakeholder data.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Diagnosis shows the hidden family, the selection mechanism, and a pre-specified repair.

stages.title: Fresh policy comparison without assistance
stages.instructions: Without AI-generated code, a support team trials a queue policy: 91/140 versus 101/140 one-day resolutions, then explores many post-hoc metrics and segments. Produce a decision note: population, estimand, rates, absolute and relative effect, SE, 95% interval, a useful null, a calibrated test interpretation, the post-hoc family, and a decision that includes operational value. A calculator and the Python standard library are allowed. Pandas is not required.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Fresh no-AI note reports estimate+interval+n, refuses certainty-from-p, and names the comparison family.

stages.title: Record an inference policy
stages.instructions: Complete an inference-policy ADR: primary metric, estimand, interval, planned comparisons, and revisit conditions. Reject treating p < 0.05 as proof and reject causal claims from correlation alone.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: ADR states a pre-specified family, interval reporting, and a causal-identification boundary.

stages.title: Connect inference instruments to V04
stages.instructions: Explain how M18 supplies V04 statistical instruments: sampling variation, standard error, confidence and bootstrap intervals, effect size with n, hypothesis tests as one input, and audit trails that keep exploration distinct from confirmation.

stages.title: Evaluate inference evidence
stages.instructions: Evaluate orientation, experiment, controlled-failure, transfer, and ADR evidence. Issue PASSED or a targeted repair plan. A bare significant/not-significant label does not pass.
